newsitem.title: USA: Dell momentum strong, no slowing in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dell momentum strong, no slowing in Europe.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp vice chairman Mort Topfer said its momentum remains strong and the company is "very pleased" with the current quarter and the momentum in the direct PC business.

Topfer, speaking in a telephone interview after a presentation at a technology investment conference, said the direct marketer of PCs is not seeing any slowdown of momentum in Europe. Topfer said this was a concern of many investors at the conference following Intel Corp's announcement of a second quarter earnings shortfall a few weeks ago.
"A number of people asked about Europe," he said.
"We are not seeing any slowing of momentum in Europe. We think there was some stuffing of the indirect channel," referring to computer distributors with too much product.
Intel cited weak demand, particulary in Europe, for its anticipated second quarter shortfall.
Topfer said that Dell's second quarter momentum remains at its typical pace, but he declined to provide any forecasts.
"Typically, in our momentum from first quarter to second we see sequential growth of three to four percent," he said, adding that he cannot make forecasts. "We are very pleased."
Dell's first quarter revenues jumped 58 percent over the year ago period, up about eight percent sequentially, he said.
